title: Ezekiel 8 — Carried by a lock of hair to the abominations in the temple

verdicts.reasoning: Date formula and wattippōl ʿālay šām yaḏ ʾăḏōnāy YHWH 'the hand of the Lord YHWH fell upon me there' exact; 'elders of Judah' in the book's English name form.

MT dəmûṯ kəmarʾēh-ʾēš 'like the appearance of fire' kept against LXX andros (ʾîš), which Zimmerli and NRSV adopt; the MT construes (cf. 1:27) and the variant is recorded. zōhar 'brightness' and chashmal as at 1:4, 27.

citations: TBWTT ch. 3 (Raëlian canon; verified against the FR/EN quotation file)
verdicts.reasoning: tabnîṯ yāḏ 'the pattern of a hand' (as signed-off 10:8), bəṣîṣiṯ rōʾšî 'by a lock of my head', 'court' supplied for the feminine happənîmîṯ (as ASV), sēmel 'image'. 'between the land and the skies' applies the ratified eretz default and the physical-space register of shamayim (same pair as GEN-WOH 1:1), and 'in visions of Elohim' keeps the Hebrew's visionary frame. Reception note accurately reports TBWTT ch. 3 and is labelled.
kəḇôḏ ʾĕlōhê yiśrāʾēl 'the glory of the Elohim of Israel' applies two central direct entries; kammarʾeh ... babbiqʿâ refers to 3:22-23. Exact.
miṣṣāp̄ôn ləšaʿar hammizbēaḥ 'north of the gate of the altar'; babbiʾâ (hapax) 'at the entrance'. Exact.

citations: Tov, Textual Criticism of the Hebrew Bible (3rd ed., 2012), on Ketiv/Qere
verdicts.reasoning: Ketiv mhm / Qere mâ hēm verified (word division); 'what they are doing' follows the Qere. Subjectless ləroḥŏqâ kept as ASV ('so that I go far') with NRSV's causative recorded.
ḥōr-ʾeḥāḏ bakkîr 'a hole in the wall'. Exact.
ḥăṯor-nāʾ ḇaqqîr 'dig now through the wall'; peṯaḥ ʾeḥāḏ 'an entrance'. Exact.
hattôʿēḇôṯ hārāʿôṯ 'the evil abominations' under central toevah. Exact.

kol-tabnîṯ remeś ûḇəhēmâ šeqeṣ: 'every pattern of creeping thing and beast, a detestable thing' keeps šeqeṣ apart from tôʿēḇâ and šiqqûṣ; gillûlîm 'idols' with derivation noted; məḥuqqeh 'engraved'. Correct.
Seventy elders, Jaazaniah son of Shaphan; miqṭartô 'his censer'; ʿăṯar (hapax) 'fragrance'. Exact; Shaphan identification correctly hedged.
bəḥaḏrê maśkîṯô 'in his chambers of imagery' (ASV); the elders' saying nested in single quotes; 'the land' under eretz. Exact.
ʿôḏ tāšûḇ tirʾeh tôʿēḇôṯ gəḏōlôṯ 'You will yet again see great abominations'. Exact.
məḇakkôṯ ʾeṯ-hattammûz 'weeping for Tammuz', article dropped as in ASV/NRSV; Dumuzi identification and Yamauchi, JBL 84 (1965) cited correctly.
hărāʾîṯā ben-ʾāḏām ... gəḏōlôṯ mēʾēlleh 'abominations greater than these'. Exact.

citations: NRSV Ezek 8:16 ('the temple of the LORD')
verdicts.reasoning: hêḵal YHWH 'the temple of YHWH': the men stand between the porch and the altar with their backs to the hêḵāl, so the referent is the building as a whole and the central entry's context clause ('temple' for the whole sanctuary) applies; this does not conflict with the Kings 'great hall', which is reserved for the main room (Ezek 41:1-4 in a later wave). The anomalous mištaḥăwîṯem rendered as participle and recorded.
MT ʾel-ʾappām 'to their nose' kept and the tiqqûn sōp̄ərîm 'to my nose' recorded (McCarthy, OBO 36); hănāqēl 'Is it too light a thing'; ḥāmās 'violence'. Correct.
lōʾ-ṯāḥôs ʿênî wəlōʾ ʾeḥmōl refrain; speech closes correctly. Exact.

glossaryReview.reasoning: inferred is the right claim type: transliteration leaves an acknowledged wind/spirit ambiguity open, and the agent/transport sites (2:2; 3:12, 14a, 24; 8:3; 11:1, 24; 43:5), the idiom 'spirit' (3:14b; 11:5b) and the compass 'side' (42:16-20) are all correctly classified and applied. reviewerReport.lensLeakageCheck: Checked every English line, with particular attention to the 16 reception-note sites (2:1, 2:10, 3:3, 3:12, 8:3, 11:1, 11:23, 40:2, 40:3, 42:14, 43:2, 44:2, 44:3, 44:15, 44:18, 44:30). No line carries the canon reading: kāḇôḏ stays 'glory' (11:23; 43:2), the bronze man keeps the Hebrew simile (40:3), qōḏeš stays 'holy' against the canon's 'healthful' (42:14), ʾûlām stays 'porch' against the 'airlock' reading (44:3), and yezaʿ is rendered by its accepted sense (44:18). Each reception note was checked against the TBWTT ch. 3 quotation file and is accurate and labelled, except that 11:23 slightly overstates the canon (verdict revise, notes only). Two features a cold reader might query were judged not to be leakage: 'ruach' (an inferred overlay convention that leaves an acknowledged ambiguity open and replaces the ASV's doctrinal capital) and 'between the land and the skies' at 8:3 (the ratified eretz default and shamayim physical register, identical to GEN-WOH 1:1, with the Hebrew's 'in visions of Elohim' kept). The sacrificial and architectural modernizations ('guilt-offering', 'dash', 'guardroom', 'vestibule', 'altar hearth') follow NRSV/NJPS and the lexica and carry no interpretive content.
reviewerReport.escalationReportAdjustments: Initial verdicts on all 207 verses, the 17 overlay entries and the 27 central-diff ops were formed from the chapters, sources, overlay, central diff and the 2.80.0 base before opening wave-e2-editor-report.md. After reading it no verdict changed. The report raises nothing on 11:19 (a new ruach), 11:23 (reception-note wording) or 44:24 (Ketiv wording in the line), so those stand. Spot-checks the report requested: NRSV 8:16 'temple', 42:1 'temple yard', 42:3 'in three stories', 43:15-16 'altar hearth', Yadin IEJ 8 (1958), the Mesha line-12 ʾrʾl, and Albright 1942 (ziggurat; arallû) are consistent with the reviewer's knowledge; the '43:3 six manuscripts' count and the exact LXX figure at 40:14 could not be confirmed independently and should be checked against BHS or worded as 'some manuscripts' / 'a different figure' (non-blocking). The report's Ketiv/Qere count (48 readings in 24 verses) matches the reviewer's independent count of 50 bracketed tokens.

founderDecisionRecommendations.A-quotation-marks: Ratify the Kings convention for Ezekiel. The reviewer's own stack simulation confirms all eight chapters balance and the 43:7-17 boundary is defensible. Schedule a punctuation-only pass on ch. 37 (37:4-5, 9, 12-14, 16, 19, 21-28) and a check of chs. 1 and 10 so the book ships with one convention.
founderDecisionRecommendations.B-proper-names: Keep English forms in Ezekiel for this wave: a mixed book would be worse than either practice, and the three signed-off chapters already use English. Recommendation for the corpus decision: the Latter Prophets volumes (isaiah-woh, ezekiel-woh, daniel-woh) already share English forms while genesis/exodus/Kings transliterate; record that genre split explicitly in a central convention note rather than converting Ezekiel, unless the founder wants decision A extended corpus-wide, in which case the mechanical pass over all eleven chapters is straightforward.
founderDecisionRecommendations.C-ruach: Ratify the overlay rule for agent/transport rûaḥ, 'spirit' for human idioms and 'side' for the compass sense, and support merging it with the Kings ruach entries into one central entry. Before promotion, narrow the 'gift' clause: rûaḥ ḥăḏāšâ paired with lēḇ (11:19; later 18:31; 36:26a) is the human disposition and should be 'a new spirit', while YHWH's own rûaḥ and the breath of life (36:27; 37:5-6, 14) stay 'ruach'. Verse flag at EZK-WOH-11:19.
founderDecisionRecommendations.D-inferred-temple-terms: Ship both as inferred. ʾêlām 'vestibule' (NRSV) and harʾēl/ʾăriʾêl 'altar hearth' (NRSV) are lexically supported, replace ASV renderings without lexical basis ('arches', 'upper altar'), and the disputes (40:30 plurals; the 'mountain of El' vocalization) are recorded.
founderDecisionRecommendations.E-sacrificial-vocabulary: Ratify the new central entry as direct. 'guilt-offering' and 'dash' are lexically motivated and match NRSV/NJPS and isaiah-woh; Milgrom's alternatives are correctly recorded but not adopted. Add the glossaryRef to EXO-WOH-20:21 and 1KI-WOH-8:63-64 at the next pass of those books.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F-refId-prefix: Agree. Normalize EZK- to EZK-WOH- (and GEN- to GEN-WOH-) in one dedicated mechanical central op with a before/after count, separate from any content diff, and only after the Revelation and Ezekiel E2 diffs are both applied.

paragraphs.text: וַיְהִ֣י ׀ בַּשָּׁנָ֣ה הַשִּׁשִּׁ֗ית בַּשִּׁשִּׁי֙ בַּחֲמִשָּׁ֣ה לַחֹ֔דֶשׁ אֲנִי֙ יוֹשֵׁ֣ב בְּבֵיתִ֔י וְזִקְנֵ֥י יְהוּדָ֖ה יוֹשְׁבִ֣ים לְפָנָ֑י וַתִּפֹּ֤ל עָלַי֙ שָׁ֔ם יַ֖ד אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהֹוִֽה׃

i18n.en: In the sixth year, in the sixth month, on the fifth of the month, as I was sitting in my house, with the elders of Judah sitting before me, the hand of the Lord YHWH fell upon me there.

notes.official: The date, the sixth year (of Jehoiachin's exile, 1:2), sixth month, fifth day, falls in September 592 BCE on the usual reckoning. *wattippōl ʿālay šām yaḏ ʾăḏōnāy YHWH* 'the hand of the Lord YHWH fell upon me there': here the hand 'falls', where elsewhere it 'is' upon him (1:3; 3:22) (`yad-yhwh`; `adonai-yhwh`). *ziqnê yəhûḏâ* 'the elders of Judah', the leaders of the exiles (cf. 14:1; 20:1).

paragraphs.text: וָאֶרְאֶ֗ה וְהִנֵּ֤ה דְמוּת֙ כְּמַרְאֵה־אֵ֔שׁ מִמַּרְאֵ֥ה מָתְנָ֛יו וּלְמַ֖טָּה אֵ֑שׁ וּמִמָּתְנָ֣יו וּלְמַ֔עְלָה כְּמַרְאֵה־זֹ֖הַר כְּעֵ֥ין הַחַשְׁמַֽלָה׃

i18n.en: I looked, and behold — a likeness like the appearance of fire: from the appearance of his loins and downward, fire; and from his loins and upward, like the appearance of brightness, like the look of *chashmal*.

notes.official:
*dəmûṯ kəmarʾēh-ʾēš* 'a likeness like the appearance of fire'. The LXX has *homoiōma andros* 'a likeness of a man', reading *ʾîš* for *ʾēš*, and NRSV and many commentators follow it ('a figure that looked like a human being'), noting the parallel at 1:26-27. The MT can be construed, and the description of loins below and above repeats 1:27, where fire is also the substance. The MT is translated (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-ezekiel`). The stacked likeness formula is kept (`mar'eh-demut`).

*kəmarʾēh-zōhar kəʿên haḥašmalâ* 'like the appearance of brightness, like the look of *chashmal*': *zōhar* is 'brightness' (Dan 12:3), and *ḥašmal* is kept in Hebrew as at 1:4, 27 (`chashmal`).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּשְׁלַח֙ תַּבְנִ֣ית יָ֔ד וַיִּקָּחֵ֖נִי בְּצִיצִ֣ת רֹאשִׁ֑י וַתִּשָּׂ֣א אֹתִ֣י ר֣וּחַ ׀ בֵּֽין־הָאָ֣רֶץ וּבֵ֣ין הַשָּׁמַ֡יִם וַתָּבֵא֩ אֹתִ֨י יְרוּשָׁלְַ֜מָה בְּמַרְא֣וֹת אֱלֹהִ֗ים אֶל־פֶּ֜תַח שַׁ֤עַר הַפְּנִימִית֙ הַפּוֹנֶ֣ה צָפ֔וֹנָה אֲשֶׁר־שָׁ֣ם מוֹשַׁ֔ב סֵ֖מֶל הַקִּנְאָ֥ה הַמַּקְנֶֽה׃

i18n.en: He stretched out the pattern of a hand and took me by a lock of my head; and ruach lifted me up between the land and the skies, and brought me to Jerusalem in visions of Elohim, to the entrance of the gate of the inner court that faces north, where the seat of the image of jealousy, which provokes jealousy, was.

notes.official:
*wayyišlaḥ tabnîṯ yāḏ* 'he stretched out the pattern of a hand': *tabnîṯ* is 'pattern, form, model' (Ex 25:9, 40). It is rendered 'pattern' as at 10:8 ('the pattern of a human hand'); ASV has 'the form of a hand' (`tabnit-toknit-tekhunah-pattern-plan-arrangement-ezekiel`). *bəṣîṣiṯ rōʾšî* 'by a lock of my head': *ṣîṣiṯ* is a tassel or fringe (Num 15:38-39), here a lock of hair.

*wattiśśāʾ ʾōṯî rûaḥ bên-hāʾāreṣ ûḇên haššāmayim* 'and ruach lifted me up between the land and the skies'. *rûaḥ* follows the book's convention (`ruach-agent-gift-and-side-ezekiel`; ASV 'the Spirit'). The pair *ʾereṣ*/*šāmayim* here marks the physical space between ground and sky. Under the register rule of `shamayim` the physical sky is 'skies', and `eretz` keeps its default 'land', which gives the same pair as genesis-woh 1:1. The ASV has 'between earth and heaven'. *bəmarʾôṯ ʾĕlōhîm* 'in visions of Elohim' (`mar'ot-elohim`; cf. 1:1; 40:2): the Hebrew presents the journey as visionary.

*šaʿar happənîmîṯ* 'the gate of the inner [court]': the adjective is feminine and qualifies an unexpressed *ḥāṣēr* 'court', so the noun is supplied, as in the ASV. *sēmel haqqinʾâ hammaqneh* 'the image of jealousy, which provokes jealousy': *sēmel* is a statue (Deut 4:16; 2 Chr 33:7, 15, Manasseh's *sēmel* in the Temple).

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** The Book Which Tells the Truth (ch. 3) quotes the verse ('the spirit lifted me up between earth and heaven, and brought me to Jerusalem') as one of Ezekiel's journeys in a flying craft of the creators. The line keeps the book's rûaḥ convention, the šāmayim register rule and the Hebrew's 'in visions of Elohim'.

paragraphs.text: וְהִ֨נֵּה־שָׁ֔ם כְּב֖וֹד אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל כַּמַּרְאֶ֕ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר רָאִ֖יתִי בַּבִּקְעָֽה׃

i18n.en: And behold — the glory of the Elohim of Israel was there, like the appearance that I had seen in the valley.

notes.official: *kəḇôḏ ʾĕlōhê yiśrāʾēl* 'the glory of the Elohim of Israel' (`kavod-yhwh`; `elohei-yisrael`). *kammarʾeh ʾăšer rāʾîṯî babbiqʿâ* 'like the appearance that I had seen in the valley' refers back to 3:22-23 (`biq'ah-ha-atzamot`).

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֔י בֶּן־אָדָ֕ם שָׂא־נָ֥א עֵינֶ֖יךָ דֶּ֣רֶךְ צָפ֑וֹנָה וָאֶשָּׂ֤א עֵינַי֙ דֶּ֣רֶךְ צָפ֔וֹנָה וְהִנֵּ֤ה מִצָּפוֹן֙ לְשַׁ֣עַר הַמִּזְבֵּ֔חַ סֵ֛מֶל הַקִּנְאָ֥ה הַזֶּ֖ה בַּבִּאָֽה׃

i18n.en: He said to me, "Son of human, lift up your eyes now toward the north." So I lifted up my eyes toward the north, and behold — north of the gate of the altar, this image of jealousy, at the entrance.

notes.official: *miṣṣāp̄ôn ləšaʿar hammizbēaḥ* 'north of the gate of the altar': the north gate of the inner court, so called because the altar stood inside it. *sēmel haqqinʾâ hazzeh babbiʾâ* 'this image of jealousy, at the entrance': *biʾâ* 'entrance' occurs only here.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֔י בֶּן־אָדָ֕ם הֲרֹאֶ֥ה אַתָּ֖ה מהם [מָ֣ה] [הֵ֣ם] עֹשִׂ֑ים תּוֹעֵב֨וֹת גְּדֹל֜וֹת אֲשֶׁ֥ר בֵּֽית־יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל ׀ עֹשִׂ֣ים פֹּ֗ה לְרָֽחֳקָה֙ מֵעַ֣ל מִקְדָּשִׁ֔י וְעוֹד֙ תָּשׁ֣וּב תִּרְאֶ֔ה תּוֹעֵב֖וֹת גְּדֹלֽוֹת׃ (ס)

i18n.en: He said to me, "Son of human, do you see what they are doing — the great abominations that the house of Israel are doing here, so that I go far from my sanctuary? But you will yet again see great abominations."

notes.official:
Ketiv/Qere: Ketiv *mhm* / Qere *mâ hēm* 'what they [are doing]', a difference of word division only; the Qere is translated (`ketiv-qere-qere-translated-ezekiel`). *tôʿēḇôṯ gəḏōlôṯ* 'great abominations' (`toevah-abomination-cross-corpus-keyword`).

*ləroḥŏqâ mēʿal miqdāšî* 'so that I go far from my sanctuary': the infinitive has no expressed subject. The ASV ('that I should go far off from my sanctuary') takes it of YHWH's departure, which chs. 10-11 narrate; NRSV makes it causative ('to drive me far from my sanctuary'). It could also mean that the practices put the people far from the sanctuary. The line keeps the ASV reading.

paragraphs.text: וַיָּבֵ֥א אֹתִ֖י אֶל־פֶּ֣תַח הֶֽחָצֵ֑ר וָאֶרְאֶ֕ה וְהִנֵּ֥ה חֹר־אֶחָ֖ד בַּקִּֽיר׃

i18n.en: He brought me to the entrance of the court, and I looked, and behold — a hole in the wall.

notes.official: *wəhinnēh ḥōr-ʾeḥāḏ bakkîr* 'behold, a hole in the wall'. The secret chamber of vv 7-12 is reached by digging (v 8).

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֔י בֶּן־אָדָ֖ם חֲתָר־נָ֣א בַקִּ֑יר וָאֶחְתֹּ֣ר בַּקִּ֔יר וְהִנֵּ֖ה פֶּ֥תַח אֶחָֽד׃

i18n.en: He said to me, "Son of human, dig now through the wall." So I dug through the wall, and behold — an entrance.

notes.official: *ḥăṯor-nāʾ ḇaqqîr* 'dig now through the wall' (*ḥāṯar* 'break through, dig', Amos 9:2; Job 24:16). *wəhinnēh peṯaḥ ʾeḥāḏ* 'behold, an entrance'.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אֵלָ֑י בֹּ֤א וּרְאֵה֙ אֶת־הַתּוֹעֵב֣וֹת הָרָע֔וֹת אֲשֶׁ֛ר הֵ֥ם עֹשִׂ֖ים פֹּֽה׃

i18n.en: He said to me, "Go in and see the evil abominations that they are doing here."

paragraphs.text: וָאָבוֹא֮ וָֽאֶרְאֶה֒ וְהִנֵּ֨ה כָל־תַּבְנִ֜ית רֶ֤מֶשׂ וּבְהֵמָה֙ שֶׁ֔קֶץ וְכָל־גִּלּוּלֵ֖י בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל מְחֻקֶּ֥ה עַל־הַקִּ֖יר סָבִ֥יב ׀ סָבִֽיב׃

i18n.en: So I went in and looked, and behold — every pattern of creeping thing and beast, a detestable thing, and all the idols of the house of Israel, engraved on the wall all around.

notes.official:
*kol-tabnîṯ remeś ûḇəhēmâ šeqeṣ* 'every pattern of creeping thing and beast, a detestable thing'. *tabnîṯ* is 'pattern' as in v 3 (`tabnit-toknit-tekhunah-pattern-plan-arrangement-ezekiel`; ASV 'every form'). *šeqeṣ* is the Priestly term for the unclean creatures of Lev 11:10-42. It is rendered 'a detestable thing' (ASV 'abominable beasts') to keep it apart from *tôʿēḇâ* 'abomination' and from the related *šiqqûṣ* (11:18, 21 'detestable things').

*kol-gillûlê bêṯ yiśrāʾēl* 'all the idols of the house of Israel'. *gillûlîm* is Ezekiel's own polemical word for idols: some forty of its roughly fifty occurrences in the Hebrew Bible are in Ezekiel. It is usually derived from *gll* and associated with *gēl* 'dung', a deliberate deformation (Zimmerli; Block, 'dung pellets'). The plain 'idols' of the ASV is kept, with the derivation recorded here (also 44:10, 12). *məḥuqqeh ʿal-haqqîr* 'engraved on the wall' (cf. 23:14).

paragraphs.text: וְשִׁבְעִ֣ים אִ֣ישׁ מִזִּקְנֵ֣י בֵֽית־יִ֠שְׂרָאֵל וְיַאֲזַנְיָ֨הוּ בֶן־שָׁפָ֜ן עֹמֵ֤ד בְּתוֹכָם֙ עֹמְדִ֣ים לִפְנֵיהֶ֔ם וְאִ֥ישׁ מִקְטַרְתּ֖וֹ בְּיָד֑וֹ וַעֲתַ֥ר עֲנַֽן־הַקְּטֹ֖רֶת עֹלֶֽה׃

i18n.en: And seventy men of the elders of the house of Israel, with Jaazaniah son of Shaphan standing among them, were standing before them, each man with his censer in his hand; and the fragrance of the cloud of incense was going up.

notes.official: *wəšiḇʿîm ʾîš mizziqnê ḇêṯ-yiśrāʾēl* 'seventy men of the elders of the house of Israel' recalls the seventy elders of Ex 24:1, 9 and Num 11:16, 24-25. *wəyaʾăzanyāhû ḇen-šāp̄ān* 'Jaazaniah son of Shaphan' (`proper-names-english-forms-convention-ezekiel`). If this Shaphan is Josiah's scribe (2 Kgs 22:3-14), whose sons supported Jeremiah (Jer 26:24; 36:10-12), the son's presence here is pointed; the identification is likely but not certain. *ʾîš miqṭartô bəyāḏô* 'each man with his censer in his hand'. *waʿăṯar ʿănan-haqqəṭōreṯ ʿōleh* 'and the fragrance of the cloud of incense was going up' (*ʿāṯār*, 'odour, fragrance', occurs only here).

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַי֮ הֲרָאִ֣יתָ בֶן־אָדָם֒ אֲשֶׁ֨ר זִקְנֵ֤י בֵֽית־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ עֹשִׂ֣ים בַּחֹ֔שֶׁךְ אִ֖ישׁ בְּחַדְרֵ֣י מַשְׂכִּית֑וֹ כִּ֣י אֹמְרִ֗ים אֵ֤ין יְהוָה֙ רֹאֶ֣ה אֹתָ֔נוּ עָזַ֥ב יְהוָ֖ה אֶת־הָאָֽרֶץ׃

i18n.en: He said to me, "Have you seen, son of human, what the elders of the house of Israel are doing in the dark, each man in his chambers of imagery? For they are saying, 'YHWH does not see us; YHWH has forsaken the land.'"

notes.official: *ʾîš bəḥaḏrê maśkîṯô* 'each man in his chambers of imagery': *maśkîṯ* is a carved figure or image (Lev 26:1 *ʾeḇen maśkîṯ*; Num 33:52); the ASV 'chambers of imagery' is kept. The elders' saying, *ʾên YHWH rōʾeh ʾōṯānû ʿāzaḇ YHWH ʾeṯ-hāʾāreṣ* 'YHWH does not see us; YHWH has forsaken the land', is quoted inside the speech in single quotes and returns at 9:9 (`eretz`).

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אֵלָ֑י ע֣וֹד תָּשׁ֥וּב תִּרְאֶ֛ה תּוֹעֵב֥וֹת גְּדֹל֖וֹת אֲשֶׁר־הֵ֥מָּה עֹשִֽׂים׃

i18n.en: He said to me, "You will yet again see great abominations that they are doing."

paragraphs.text: וַיָּבֵ֣א אֹתִ֗י אֶל־פֶּ֙תַח֙ שַׁ֣עַר בֵּית־יְהוָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֖ר אֶל־הַצָּפ֑וֹנָה וְהִנֵּה־שָׁם֙ הַנָּשִׁ֣ים יֹֽשְׁב֔וֹת מְבַכּ֖וֹת אֶת־הַתַּמּֽוּז׃ (ס)

i18n.en: He brought me to the entrance of the gate of the house of YHWH that is toward the north, and behold — there the women were sitting, weeping for Tammuz.

notes.official: *wəhinnēh-šām hannāšîm yōšəḇôṯ məḇakkôṯ ʾeṯ-hattammûz* 'and behold — there the women were sitting, weeping for Tammuz'. Tammuz is the Mesopotamian Dumuzi, the shepherd-god mourned in the summer month that bears his name (Jacobsen, *The Treasures of Darkness*, 1976; Yamauchi, 'Tammuz and the Bible', *JBL* 84, 1965). The Hebrew has the article (*hattammûz*, as with *habbaʿal*); English convention drops it, as do the ASV and NRSV (`proper-names-english-forms-convention-ezekiel`). The central `dumuzi-tammuz-adonis-dying-and-rising-vegetation-god-cross-corpus` governs the Akkadian sources and not this Hebrew line, but its rationale describes the cult.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר אֵלַ֖י הֲרָאִ֣יתָ בֶן־אָדָ֑ם ע֣וֹד תָּשׁ֥וּב תִּרְאֶ֛ה תּוֹעֵב֥וֹת גְּדֹל֖וֹת מֵאֵֽלֶּה׃

i18n.en: He said to me, "Have you seen, son of human? You will yet again see abominations greater than these."

paragraphs.text: וַיָּבֵ֣א אֹתִ֗י אֶל־חֲצַ֣ר בֵּית־יְהוָה֮ הַפְּנִימִית֒ וְהִנֵּה־פֶ֜תַח הֵיכַ֣ל יְהוָ֗ה בֵּ֤ין הָֽאוּלָם֙ וּבֵ֣ין הַמִּזְבֵּ֔חַ כְּעֶשְׂרִ֥ים וַחֲמִשָּׁ֖ה אִ֑ישׁ אֲחֹ֨רֵיהֶ֜ם אֶל־הֵיכַ֤ל יְהוָה֙ וּפְנֵיהֶ֣ם קֵ֔דְמָה וְהֵ֛מָּה מִשְׁתַּחֲוִיתֶ֥ם קֵ֖דְמָה לַשָּֽׁמֶשׁ׃

i18n.en: He brought me into the inner court of the house of YHWH, and behold — at the entrance of the temple of YHWH, between the porch and the altar, about twenty-five men, with their backs toward the temple of YHWH and their faces toward the east; and they were bowing down eastward to the sun.

notes.official:
*peṯaḥ hêḵal YHWH bên hāʾûlām ûḇên hammizbēaḥ* 'at the entrance of the temple of YHWH, between the porch and the altar'. Under `ulam-hekhal-devir-temple-three-room-plan-cross-corpus`, *hêḵāl* is 'great hall' when it names the main room of the three-room plan, and 'temple' when it names the sanctuary as a whole. Here the men stand in the court in front of the porch, between it and the altar (cf. Joel 2:17), with 'their backs toward the *hêḵāl*'. What they turn their backs on is the building as seen from the court, so the context clause gives 'temple' (so also NRSV and NJPS here). *ʾûlām* is 'porch' as the entry rules.

*wəhēmmâ mištaḥăwîṯem qēḏmâ laššāmeš* 'and they were bowing down eastward to the sun'. *mištaḥăwîṯem* is an anomalous form that mixes the participle with a second-person perfect ending; some explain it as a scribal blend, others as a deliberate distortion. It is rendered as the participle (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-ezekiel`). On sun worship in the Temple court see 2 Kgs 23:5, 11.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַי֮ הֲרָאִ֣יתָ בֶן־אָדָם֒ הֲנָקֵל֙ לְבֵ֣ית יְהוּדָ֔ה מֵעֲשׂ֕וֹת אֶת־הַתּוֹעֵב֖וֹת אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָֽשׂוּ־פֹ֑ה כִּֽי־מָלְא֨וּ אֶת־הָאָ֜רֶץ חָמָ֗ס וַיָּשֻׁ֙בוּ֙ לְהַכְעִיסֵ֔נִי וְהִנָּ֛ם שֹׁלְחִ֥ים אֶת־הַזְּמוֹרָ֖ה אֶל־אַפָּֽם׃

i18n.en: He said to me, "Have you seen, son of human? Is it too light a thing for the house of Judah to do the abominations that they have done here, that they have filled the land with violence and have provoked me to anger again? And behold, they are putting the branch to their nose.

notes.official: *wəhinnām šōləḥîm ʾeṯ-hazzəmôrâ ʾel-ʾappām* 'and behold, they are putting the branch to their nose'. The rite is unknown; *zəmôrâ* is a cut branch or vine-shoot (Num 13:23; Isa 17:10). Rabbinic tradition lists this verse among the *tiqqûnê sōp̄ərîm*, the scribal corrections, and says the original text read 'to my nose' (McCarthy, *The Tiqqune Sopherim*, OBO 36, 1981). The transmitted text, 'their nose', is translated (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-ezekiel`). *kî-mālʾû ʾeṯ-hāʾāreṣ ḥāmās* 'that they have filled the land with violence' (`eretz`; cf. Gen 6:11, 13).

paragraphs.text: וְגַם־אֲנִי֙ אֶעֱשֶׂ֣ה בְחֵמָ֔ה לֹֽא־תָח֥וֹס עֵינִ֖י וְלֹ֣א אֶחְמֹ֑ל וְקָרְא֤וּ בְאָזְנַי֙ ק֣וֹל גָּד֔וֹל וְלֹ֥א אֶשְׁמַ֖ע אוֹתָֽם׃

i18n.en: Therefore I too will act in wrath; my eye shall not spare, and I will have no pity; and though they cry in my ears with a loud voice, I will not hear them."

notes.official: *lōʾ-ṯāḥôs ʿênî wəlōʾ ʾeḥmōl* 'my eye shall not spare, and I will have no pity' is a refrain of Ezekiel's judgment oracles (5:11; 7:4, 9; 9:10). *wəqārəʾû ḇəʾāznay qôl gāḏôl* 'though they cry in my ears with a loud voice'. The speech that began in 8:17 closes here.
